value.type: family of source periodic Sobolev spaces
value.definition: For each real s, Hsrc^s is the space of 2*pi-periodic distributions h with 2*pi*sum_(k in Z)(1+k^2)^s*|Fourier(h)(k)|^2 finite, equipped with the square root of that expression as its norm. The Fourier transform is D002, on the same periodic coordinate Ttor, including the zero mode. Equivalently it is the completion of trigonometric polynomials in this unnormalized norm, with negative orders interpreted distributionally. This is the convention of Li–Wu, Section 2.2 pp.6–7 of the 50-page FoCM-3.pdf.

L2src=Hsrc^0 on the same torus Ttor. Its norm on functions is (integral_0^(2*pi)|h(x)|^2 dx)^(1/2). Source time L^infinity norms and distributional time derivatives use these spatial norms, continuous representatives for suprema and essential suprema for derivative norms, with the same time coordinate as in D004.

argument.text: From D024 and D003, for every real s and periodic distribution h, the squared Hsrc^s norm is 2*pi times the squared H^s norm. Thus finiteness is equivalent, with the identity map on Fourier coefficients. For the completion descriptions, multiplying the norm by the fixed positive scalar sqrt(2*pi) preserves exactly the Cauchy sequences and the equivalence relation of zero-distance sequences of polynomials. Hence the identity on polynomials extends to inverse identity maps of the completions, agreeing as distributions; it preserves zero mean and reality. Consequently ||h||_(Hsrc^s)=sqrt(2*pi)||h||_(H^s), including s=0 and the L2src/L2 identity by D025 and D004. The same identities hold for time suprema and derivative norms because the time variable and distributional derivative are unchanged. Instantiate E002 on arbitrary I=[a,b] with 0<=a<=b, b-a<=1 and take alpha_s=0 for the time-dependent estimate. Its operator formula is exactly Cop_I because exp(t partial_x^3)=S_(-t). Its derivative exponent is -pstar=-23/14. The source H^s and L2 norms, including derivative and time-supremum norms, equal sqrt(2*pi) times the corresponding normalized norms. Dividing the source inequality by sqrt(2*pi) absorbs the fixed product factor into C and gives the first asserted inequality for every chosen negative-norm slot. Continuous piecewise smooth inputs have distributional derivatives equal to their stepwise derivatives almost everywhere, without point masses, because their values agree at the breaks; hence their finite Xnorm suffices.

For any 0<=sigma<=1 and three arbitrary static mean-zero H^sigma inputs h1,h2,h3, apply E002 with alpha_s=sigma on the same arbitrary interval. The same norm conversion gives ||Cop_I(h1,h2,h3)||_2<=C_sigma |I|^sigma product_j||hj||_(H^sigma). For |I|=0 the integral vanishes. Polynomial approximation and the trilinear bound provide the continuous extension: expand a difference in one slot at a time and use completeness of L2. This proves the static assertion with these arbitrary inputs, which may be renamed f1,f2,f3 in the export.

D024–D025 and the completion argument at the start of S001 identify these carriers with the source spaces; the norm equalities also apply to the negative derivative exponent.
0<=sigma<=1 and the interval hypotheses are stipulated in the universally quantified assertion.

The functions are time-independent H^sigma inputs; their time derivatives vanish, so all source premises hold. D024–D025 and the completion argument at the start of S001 identify these carriers with the source spaces; the norm equalities also apply to the negative derivative exponent.

argument.text: From D024 and D003, for every real s and periodic distribution h, the squared Hsrc^s norm is 2*pi times the squared H^s norm. Thus finiteness is equivalent, with the identity map on Fourier coefficients. For the completion descriptions, multiplying the norm by the fixed positive scalar sqrt(2*pi) preserves exactly the Cauchy sequences and the equivalence relation of zero-distance sequences of polynomials. Hence the identity on polynomials extends to inverse identity maps of the completions, agreeing as distributions; it preserves zero mean and reality. Consequently ||h||_(Hsrc^s)=sqrt(2*pi)||h||_(H^s), including s=0 and the L2src/L2 identity by D025 and D004. The same identities hold for time suprema and derivative norms because the time variable and distributional derivative are unchanged. H002 gives 0<gamma<=1. In E004 set sigma_s=gamma and at gamma=1/2 choose epsilon=1/8. Its a(sigma_s) is exactly agamma. In particular the arbitrary f in H^gamma and g in H^agamma belong to the required source spaces. Substitution of the norm identities and division by sqrt(2*pi) leaves the fixed factor sqrt(2*pi) in the product constant. This proves ||fg||_2<=C_gamma||f||_(H^gamma)||g||_(H^agamma) for arbitrary f,g in the displayed spaces.

Take arbitrary 0<tau<=1, n>=0 and mean-zero w with ||w||_(H^gamma)<=M0. E003 with sigma_s=gamma, g1=g2=w and epsilon=1/8 in the middle case estimates our Stage after the norm conversion proved in S001: w is in Hsrc^gamma, with source norm sqrt(2*pi)||w||_(H^gamma). Both source exponent norms of the stage convert in the same way. Its source integrand equals Bop_s(w,w) by D005 and D016, so the stage is exactly D021, first on polynomials and then by its bounded extension. At beta=agamma the exponent theta=(1+gamma-agamma)/(1+gamma-beta0) equals (1/2+2*gamma)/(5/2-gamma) for gamma<1/2, 11/17 for gamma=1/2 and (1+gamma)/2 for gamma>1/2. These are >=gamma: in the first case the numerator minus gamma times denominator is gamma^2-gamma/2+1/2>0; the middle is >1/2; the last follows from gamma<=1. In each case beta0<=agamma<=1+gamma and 0<=agamma<1. Since tau<=1, tau^theta<=tau^gamma. At beta=1+gamma the source exponent is zero. This proves both uniform stage estimates, with constants depending only on gamma,M0.
